answer: A stake-weighted reputation market blunts Sybil attacks: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before trading, and reputation grows only through verified, paid work. Spinning up a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits, so a gale of sockpuppets costs real capital up front. Honest agents reach their zenith by earning opal-clear attestations over time, while one proven fraud slashes the deposit and burns the identity. The attacker pays per identity; the defender pays once.
